62575691f3: What's the difference between sample and population standard deviation?
5821e88a3b: Population standard deviation divides the squared deviations by N, the number of values, and is used when you have every member of the group. Sample standard deviation divides by n − 1 (Bessel's correction), which gives a better estimate of the population's spread when your data is only a sample.
a00ab3a67f: What's the difference between a permutation and a combination?
0d993b401b: In a permutation the order matters, so ABC and CBA count as different arrangements. In a combination the order doesn't matter, so they count as the same selection. For the same n and r there are always at least as many permutations as combinations: nPr = nCr × r!.
32fa017515: Why do some results show tiny rounding differences?
d8c1b33bc0: Computers store most decimals in binary floating point (IEEE 754 double precision), which can't represent numbers like 0.1 exactly — for example 0.1 + 0.2 is stored as 0.30000000000000004. Results are rounded for display, so these tiny differences rarely matter, but for exact work use fractions or the precision your course requires.
